title: Autumn oxygen fell on density 26.5 along the Bermuda-Puerto Rico transect between 2000-2011 and 2012-2021
abstract: We tested whether the BATS density-class thickness relation transfers to separate surveys. The planned bottle test had no repeated joint oxygen-thickness support on density 26.5 after 2011. A declared follow-up used dense BVAL CTD profiles from 13 early and 10 late autumn cruises. In seven matched cells more than 100 km from BATS, AOU rose by 7.42 umol/kg (95% cruise-bootstrap interval 3.06-11.69) and oxygen fell by 7.10. The unchanged pre-2010 BATS thickness slope predicts 3.59 of the AOU rise. The residual is 3.82 (0.91-6.70). The cruise-mean CTD-minus-bottle oxygen offset changed by -0.98 umol/kg. Applying this as a fixed error correction leaves an AOU rise of 6.44 but moves the residual interval across zero. Thus the regional loss extends beyond BATS, while evidence for an extra process beyond thickness is limited by calibration and transfer assumptions. The study uses sparse surveys, fixed spatial cells, a fixed BATS slope and no causal oxygen budget. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and a retained coverage failure permit reproduction.

display.caption: Matched autumn AOU changes and predictions from fixed BATS thickness slopes. Error bars are conditional 95% cruise-bootstrap intervals. Sensor offsets and training-slope uncertainty are excluded.
Paired AOU changes in spatial cells with at least two cruises in both epochs. Density classes share surveys and are not independent tests.
